# Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2024 Summary

The Liberal Democrats' 2024 manifesto centres on five key themes: economy, public services, environment, international relations, and democratic reform.

## Economy and Business

The party proposes investing in renewable energy and home insulation to reduce energy bills and create jobs. They would replace business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy, expand apprenticeships, and introduce Lifelong Skills Grants of £5,000 for adult education. The manifesto commits to responsible fiscal management while repairing trade relationships with Europe. Tax proposals include reversing bank tax cuts, increasing the Digital Services Tax to 6%, and reforming capital gains tax.

## Healthcare and Social Care

The manifesto promises a right to see a GP within seven days (24 hours for urgent cases), requiring 8,000 additional GPs. It guarantees NHS dental access for urgent care and proposes mental health hubs in every community. Cancer treatment would begin within 62 days of referral. For social care, the party proposes free personal care based on the Scottish model, a Carer's Minimum Wage (£2/hour above standard minimum wage), and increased support for unpaid carers including paid carer's leave.

## Education

Proposals include placing mental health professionals in every school, increasing per-pupil funding above inflation, providing tutoring guarantees for disadvantaged pupils, and reinstating maintenance grants for university students. Early years investment would include extra free hours for disadvantaged three and four-year-olds.

## Environment

The party commits to net zero by 2045, with 90% renewable electricity by 2030. A ten-year home energy upgrade programme would provide free insulation and heat pumps for low-income households. Water companies would be transformed into public benefit companies, with bonuses banned until sewage discharges end. Targets include doubling protected areas, wildlife habitats, species abundance, and woodland cover by 2050.

## Housing

The manifesto targets 380,000 new homes annually, including 150,000 social homes, through ten new garden cities. Proposals include banning no-fault evictions, creating three-year default tenancies, abolishing residential leasehold, and ending rough sleeping within the Parliament.

## Crime and Justice

Community policing would be restored with guaranteed investigation of all burglaries. A new Online Crime Agency would tackle internet-based crime. The party proposes halving the time from offence to sentencing and adopting a public health approach to youth violence.

## Immigration

The manifesto would scrap the Rwanda scheme and Illegal Migration Act, establish safe legal routes for refugees, and process asylum claims within three months. Asylum seekers could work after three months. Work visa policy would move from the Home Office to relevant departments.

## Democratic Reform

Key proposals include proportional representation via Single Transferable Vote for MPs and English councillors, votes at 16, capping political donations, and enshrining the Ministerial Code in law. The House of Lords would be reformed with a democratic mandate, and a federal UK constitution would be developed.

## Defence and International

Defence spending would increase toward 2.5% of GDP, with Army cuts reversed. The party supports NATO, Ukraine, and maintaining the nuclear deterrent. International development spending would return to 0.7% of national income. The manifesto outlines a four-stage roadmap to repair EU relations, ultimately aiming for Single Market membership as a step toward EU membership.

## Families and Welfare

Statutory Maternity Pay would double to £350 weekly, with extended paternity leave at 90% of earnings. Free school meals would extend to all children in poverty. The two-child benefit limit and benefit cap would be removed, and the triple lock on pensions maintained.
